question: Which organisation releases the official poverty estimates in India based on data collected from the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) and other sources ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** NITI Aayog releases official poverty estimates in India using data from the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO**).
 
• The **NITI Aayog is a task force that calculates the poverty line based on the data collected by the NSSO.**
 
• The NITI Aayog **is the successor to the Planning Commission of India. **
 
• The NITI Aayog **also uses data from other sources, such as the National Family Health Survey (NFHS), to estimate multidimensional poverty. **
 
• **The NITI Aayog releases the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report, w**hich tracks India's progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Poverty Estimation: 

 
• ​A common method used to estimate poverty in India is based on the income or consumption levels and if the income or consumption falls below a given minimum level, then the household is said to be Below the Poverty Line (BPL).
 
• The number of people living below the poverty line is used to calculate the poverty rate, which is the percentage of the population that is poor.
